title: Pricing by hours per project for short-stay turnover
audience: Owners and cleaners who run short-stay turnovers and need to build a price for each turnover from hours, cost and margin.
learningOutcomes: Calculate a cost per productive hour from the owner's own figures
Estimate project hours, including set-up, travel and checking time
Build a quote from hours, a rate and a margin, and state its basis and exclusions

instruction.heading: Why hours are the starting unit for a turnover
instruction.body: A turnover is a short, repeated job: the cleaner's time on site, the trip between properties, set-up, pack-down and a checking pass. Because turnovers repeat, small errors in time add up across a month. Start from hours so each turnover shows its cost, its margin and the effect of a scope change. The vendor fee bands for turnovers are references (Beyond Pricing, 28 October 2026), not your costs.

instruction.heading: Build the cost per productive hour
instruction.body: Divide the year's total business costs by chargeable hours. Include wages with on-costs where you employ staff, plus vehicle running costs, chemicals and linen handling, equipment, insurance and admin. Business.gov.au says on-costs such as super, leave and tax belong in the hourly figure (1 October 2026). Xero Australia advises dividing by billable hours, not total hours (3 September 2026). Jobber's cleaning guide puts on-costs at 25 to 40 per cent of wages, but it is US-leaning, so it is not an Australian rate.

instruction.heading: Estimate the hours for a turnover
instruction.body: Break the turnover into rooms and tasks, time each at a standard speed from past turnovers, and add set-up, pack-down, travel between properties and a checking pass as named lines. Add a set allowance for late checkouts, missing supplies and other delays. Xero Australia suggests 10 to 20 per cent for unexpected work, which is its own range and not a short-stay benchmark. Record actual hours for each turnover.

instruction.heading: Turn hours into a price and test it against the band
instruction.body: Multiply the crew hours by the cost per productive hour, then add a margin for the risk in the job, such as a heavy clean after a large group. Compare the price with the vendor band for the property size (general two-bedroom: $90 to $130 per turnover, Beyond Pricing). The band is a check, not a target. If your price is above it, show the scope that justifies it. Do not cut the cost to meet the band.

instruction.heading: Keep the quote honest
instruction.body: The quote states the checklist, the hours basis, the turnover window, exclusions, what the host must provide (linen, consumables, access codes), and validity. Business Queensland suggests charging unplanned extra costs at cost plus a stated percentage; it suggests 15 per cent, which is a suggestion, not a benchmark (16 November 2022). Price any extra turnover task in writing before it is done.

procedure: Gather the year's total costs and chargeable hours for the same period, with a source for each figure.
Divide total costs by chargeable hours and date the cost per productive hour.
Break each turnover into rooms and tasks, and estimate each as a range from timed past turnovers.
Add set-up, pack-down, travel between properties and checking as named lines.
Multiply crew hours by the cost per productive hour, add the margin, then compare with the vendor band.
Write the quote with checklist, hours basis, turnover window, exclusions, host inputs and validity.
Record actual hours after each turnover and review the variance each month.

workedExamples.situation: [ILLUSTRATIVE] A cleaner quotes a turnover for a two-bedroom apartment. Estimate: 1.5 hours on site, 0.25 hours set-up, 0.25 hours checking and 0.25 hours travel, which is 2.25 crew-hours. Cost per productive hour is $55 (illustrative; not sourced). Target margin is 25 per cent of price (illustrative).
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the cost and the price, and how does the price compare with the vendor band?
workedExamples.reasoning: The cost is 2.25 x $55, which is $123.75 (illustrative). A 25 per cent margin on price means the price is the cost divided by 0.75, which is $165.00 (CALC). The Beyond Pricing general band for a two-bedroom turnover is $90 to $130 (vendor, 28 October 2026). The cost-based price is above the band, so the cleaner tests the hours and the scope before quoting. The cleaner also checks whether the 1.5 on-site hours are real, and shows the checklist the price covers. Floor check: the Cleaning Services Award Level 1 adult minimum of $25.85 an hour, with 25 per cent casual loading, is $32.31 an hour (Fair Work Commission; 1 July 2025 variation). At that floor, 2.25 hours is $72.70 before on-costs, so the floor is not the cost per hour.

equipmentAndPpe: Time log for each job, with estimated and actual columns
Measuring tape or laser measure for area estimates

commonErrors.error: Pricing from the hourly wage alone.
commonErrors.prevention: Include on-costs, vehicle, chemicals, equipment, insurance and admin in the cost per productive hour.
Add travel as a named line on every turnover, especially when a cleaner covers several properties in one day.

commonErrors.error: Cutting the cost per hour to fit a vendor band.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the hours and the scope first. Show what the band leaves out.

commonErrors.error: Quoting with no checklist, turnover window or exclusions.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the checklist, the window and the exclusions into the quote.

commonErrors.error: Never comparing estimated and actual hours.
commonErrors.prevention: Record actual hours for each turnover and review the variance monthly.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Pricing guidance only. The Australian Consumer Law applies to price statements, and the ACCC says misleading statements about prices are prohibited (ACCC, 15 July 2026). State rules differ, so check your state's fair trading rules.

Where you employ cleaners, the Cleaning Services Award (MA000022) may set their minimum rates. The Level 1 adult minimum was $25.85 an hour from 1 July 2025, with a 25 per cent casual loading. The 2026-27 rates were not checked.
The Victorian short-stay levy is a registration duty for hosts and platforms, not a cleaning cost. Check with the host who pays it before you add anything to your price (SRO Victoria, 4 March 2025).

qualityStandard: Each quote shows scope, hours or price basis, exclusions, client inputs and validity.
The cost per productive hour is calculated from the owner's own records and dated.
Actual hours are recorded for at least the first ten jobs of each type and compared with the estimate.
No quote is issued without a margin decision and a minimum-charge check.
documentationEvidence: Cost per productive hour worksheet, dated, with the source of each figure
Quote showing scope, hours basis, exclusions and validity
Job time log with estimated and actual hours
summary: Start every turnover quote from measured hours and a cost per chargeable hour.
Name travel, set-up and checking time, and state the checklist and window in writing.
Gaps: turnover cost data, the levy rate and 2026-27 award rates were not confirmed. The vendor bands are references only.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which costs belong in the cost per productive hour for a turnover crew?
options: Only the hourly wage of the lowest-paid worker
Wages with on-costs, vehicle, chemicals, equipment, insurance and admin, divided by chargeable hours
The price the host pays, plus any deposit taken
The rate a competitor advertises for a holiday home

knowledgeChecks.question: A turnover is estimated at 2 crew-hours and takes 3. What should you do?
options: Record the actual hours, find the cause, and adjust the estimate and future quotes
Leave the estimate, because the host has paid
Cut the crew's breaks on the next turnover
Raise the price for this host only and change nothing else

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does a turnover quote need a checklist and a turnover window?
options: To show what the price covers and when the unit will be ready, so changes can be priced
To make the quote longer for the host
To hide the margin from the host
To lower the host's expectations of the turnover

sourceReferences: business.gov.au, 'Choose a pricing strategy', https://business.gov.au/products-and-services/choose-a-pricing-strategy, page metadata dated 1 October 2026. Supports: on-costs such as super, leave and tax belong in the hourly figure.

Xero Australia, 'How to price services', https://www.xero.com/au/guides/how-to-price-services/, dated 3 September 2026. Supports: divide by billable hours, not total hours; add a set allowance for delays; the guide's 10 to 20 per cent range for unexpected work is the source's own figure.

Jobber Academy, 'How Much to Charge for House Cleaning', https://getjobber.com/academy/cleaning/how-much-to-charge-for-house-cleaning/, 31 March 2026 (first published June 2023). US-leaning source. Supports: cleaners often undercount on-costs such as payroll tax, workers' compensation and unpaid travel, which the source puts at 25 to 40 per cent of wages; a profit factor on cost; annual price reviews; a flat or minimum-hours charge for short cleaning jobs.

Beyond Pricing, 'Short-term rental cleaning fees (Australia)', https://beyondpricing.com/au/blog/how-much-should-you-charge-for-cleaning-fees-in-your-australian-holiday-rental, dated 28 October 2026. Vendor source; short-stay fee data. Supports: per-turnover bands by property size; move-in and move-out bands by bedroom count; a $120 per-turnover illustration; city labour benchmarks; fixed rates suit smaller properties and hourly rates suit larger or luxury homes.

ACCC, 'Setting prices: what's allowed', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/pricing/setting-prices-whats-allowed, page last modified 15 July 2026. Supports: misleading statements about prices are prohibited.

Fair Work Commission, Cleaning Services Award (MA000022), https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000022.html, variation effective 1 July 2025. Supports: Level 1 adult minimum hourly rate of $25.85 and a 25 per cent casual loading. The 1 July 2026 position was not checked.

Business Queensland, 'Preparing a business quote: tips', https://www.business.qld.gov.au/running-business/marketing-sales/sales/preparing-quote/tips, last updated 16 November 2022. Queensland. Supports: list add-ons and alternatives on the quote; charge extra costs at cost plus a stated percentage (the source suggests 15 per cent, which is not a benchmark); follow up 7 to 14 days after the quote; confirm scope, capacity and deadline before quoting.

State Revenue Office Victoria, 'Register now for the short-stay levy', https://sro.vic.gov.au/news/register-now-short-stay-levy, published 4 March 2025. Victoria. Supports: the levy applies to stays under 28 consecutive days from 1 January 2025; booking platforms and owners or tenants who accept bookings directly must register. The page does not state the rate.
Notes: $55 an hour, the hours and the 25 per cent margin are illustrative and not sourced. The $90 to $130 band is a vendor reference for turnovers.
